# gpu slider

> A slider for the web that draws its media on a canvas and owns its motion: with WebGPU where the browser has it, with WebGL 2 where not. The core is a few kilobytes; arrows, keys, autoplay, the canvas, every effect, the lightbox and the loading screen are plugins that a page imports when it uses them. No dependencies. On npm: `npm install gpuslider`.

## Docs

- [All of the docs in one file](/llms-full.txt): DOCS.md, in Markdown
- [Get started](/docs/): the markup, what to import, and the three tiers
- [Without a script](/docs/html/): `auto.js` and attributes in the HTML, buttons anywhere
- [React](/docs/react/): the components `<Slider>` and `<Slide>`, `useSliderContext()` for what is in a slider, and the hook `useSlider` for markup of your own
- [Layout](/docs/layout/): slides per view and gap as CSS, downwards, rows, the focus point
- [Options, API and events](/docs/options/)
- [Plugins](/docs/plugins/): the ones that come with it, and how to write one
- [The canvas](/docs/canvas/): WebGPU and WebGL 2, and what they were measured at
- [Effects and transitions](/docs/effects/): all of them, and how to write one in GLSL
- [Lightbox](/docs/lightbox/)
- [Loading](/docs/loading/): a screen while the media load, and its events
- [Extending](/docs/extending/): plugins, effects, slides placed by a script with `draw()`, the types, and a list for agents
- [Community plugins](/docs/community/): plugins and effects that others have written, and how to publish one with the keyword `gpuslider-plugin`
- [Size, and what is not there yet](/docs/size/)

## Examples

- [All of them](/examples/): each with what it is made of and its code
- [Panes](/examples/panes/): four pictures in view that turn into the next ones by a transition in three ways: place by place (`panes()`), all at once in one sweep (`sweep()`), or at the edges of a row that moves (`edges()`)
- [Resolve](/examples/resolve/): rows of photos that come out part by part as they come into view, in nine ways
- [Reveal](/examples/reveal/): an index whose pictures open out of the pointer and turn into each other, in eleven ways
- [Orbit](/examples/orbit/): a row rolled up into a cylinder that the page turns as it is scrolled
- [Echo](/examples/echo/): a reel whose photos leave frames of themselves behind as they move
- [Fold](/examples/fold/): walls of small pictures that fold into place one after another as the page is scrolled
- [A reel](/examples/reel/): pictures and films as large as the screen, that the page scrolls down through
- [Tape](/examples/tape/): rows that run against each other, pushed by the scrolling
- [Loom](/examples/loom/): portraits that come apart into threads at the edges
- [Wave](/examples/wave/): bands of pictures on five pages, each wilder than the last
- [Depth](/examples/depth/): parallax, with a panel that changes it while it runs
- [Journal](/examples/journal/): a slider whose pictures open into stories on other pages, by a view transition between documents
- [Playground](/playground/): every slider the library can be, with controls

## Use

- `import { createSlider } from 'gpuslider'`: the core
- `import { controls, keyboard, wheel, autoplay, marquee, thumbs, videos, autoHeight, stack, panes, progress, loading } from 'gpuslider/plugins'`
- `import { canvas } from 'gpuslider/canvas'`: the canvas, which chooses its layer
- `import { stretch, split, waves, liquid } from 'gpuslider/effects'`: effects and transitions
- `import { gpu } from 'gpuslider/gpu'`, `import { gl } from 'gpuslider/gl'`: a layer by name
- `import { lightbox } from 'gpuslider/lightbox'`
- `import { Slider, Slide, useSliderContext, useSlider } from 'gpuslider/react'`
- `import { createSlider } from 'gpuslider/full'`: the core with all plugins, by options
